title: Darkhorse allocator fallback and KV reshard hotfix for cross-tenant OOM cascade
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A multi-tenant cascade of GPU OOMs and long-tail memory fragmentation was triggered by a combination of the Darkhorse allocator's fallback path and a rare KV cache index split race in the prefix eviction code. The issue impacted hosted and dedicated customers intermittently and caused one high-severity escalation from a major PLG customer with sustained 95th percentile latency spikes and occasional request failures.

What happened:
- Under a workload with high fanout long-context requests, allocator fragmentation caused per-session arenas to return unusable slabs to the global pool. When the allocator hit a soft failure it took the Darkhorse fallback path which attempted aggressive coalescing; coalescing triggered a reshard attempt when paired with concurrent KV-compact activity.
- A previously unseen race in the KV cache index split code allowed two concurrent reshard operations to create inconsistent tombstone pointers for recent session entries. That led to SKV (session KV) iterator returning duplicate indices and a missed reclaim of some GPU pages. Over time the allocator reported high external fragmentation, and the runtime started evicting active KV slots which caused downstream retries and, ultimately, GPU OOMs when multiple large requests coincided.

Impact:
- Hosted: transient 5-10% error rate in token generation and latency spikes for affected models during the incident window.
- Dedicated: two customer clusters reported persistent higher tail latency and one cluster experienced a cascade of OOM restarts requiring manual shard recomposition.
- Private: a large regulated customer on-prem reported an outage for a Canary service; they required our team to provide a hotpatch bundle.

Root cause (summary):
- Darkhorse allocator fallback path lacks a proper coordination barrier for simultaneous coalescing and KV reshard operations.
- KV cache split/reshard code did not update tombstone pointers atomically with respect to the KV index snapshot used by session iterators.
- Combined, these created unreclaimed GPU pages and transient double-free-like conditions that looked like fragmentation and caused the allocator to fail its slow-path assumptions.

Mitigation applied during incident:
- Short-term: increased per-tenant KV eviction aggressiveness, reduced default per-session arena size, and enabled conservative allocator backoff to reduce coalescing attempts. Deployed as platform flags for hosted and a hotpatch for dedicated/private customers.
- Customer-facing: issued priority status updates, provided a custom hotpatch tarball for the on-prem customer, and opened temporary CAP on Dedicated nodes to drain affected shards.

Permanent fix (PR linked below):
- Add a lightweight coordination barrier in the allocator between coalesce and fallback flows to serialize coalescing with active reshard operations.
- Make KV index split/reshard tombstone updates atomic by switching to a compare-and-swap commit + versioned index snapshot so iterators never observe partially-updated tombstones.
- Improve metrics and alerts for allocator fragment ratio and orphaned GPU pages; add a canary that replays long-context fanout traffic and tracks leak metrics.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit and fuzz tests for KV split under concurrent compaction + iterator usage (added 12 new tests).
- Integration test matrix across hosted->dedicated->private: simulate fanout 50 requests with max-seq 32k across multi-tenant shape to reproduce leak locally.
- Staged rollout: canary on runtime-1.25 in non-prod, then progressive rollout to low-traffic Hosted pools, Limited Dedicated clusters, then full rollout. Rollback runbook validated.

Operational tasks and follow-ups:
- Postmortem doc and RCA due 2026-03-20.
- Add automatic shard-health reconciler to Console to detect incomplete reshard state (PM ticket requested).
- Run a one-week retro replay of long-context fanout workloads across Dedicated clusters (reliability engineering).
- Customer success to follow up with affected customers and provide credits or SLA adjustments as needed.

References and artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421 (allocator barrier + kv atomic commit)
- Hotpatch bundle sent to on-prem customer: gs://redwood-hotpatches/2026-03-darkhorse-kv-80722.tar.gz
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/oom-cascade-2026-03
